haiku-low.q1: They land in the same account. Matching uses the Google sub, which stays linked, and the email is not checked. Google never changes users.email.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the existing password at /auth/google/confirm. After a correct bcrypt check, the link is inserted, the pending record deleted, and then the session starts.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds to failed_logins. The 5th locks the account for 15 minutes and deletes the pending link, so the user must restart Google sign-in.
haiku-low.q4: An unmatched verified email creates a user with NULL password, a linked identity and a session, in one transaction. Unverified email redirects to /login telling the user to use email and password.
haiku-low.q5: Both fail with the error page. The attempt expires after 10 minutes, and a repeated callback finds the record already consumed by GETDEL. Nothing is written.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row and a new sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days). The old sessions row for any existing sid is deleted first.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required in link mode. The session user must match the attempt user_id. If the Google account belongs to another user, Settings shows it is linked to another account.
haiku-low.q8: The state, nonce, PKCE verifier and next are stored in Redis as oidc:attempt:STATE with a 10-minute TTL. The callback's atomic GETDEL removes them; unused records expire.
haiku-low.q9: Redis oidc:pending:ID holds user_id, google_sub, google_email and next. The browser holds only the random ID in an HttpOnly, Secure pending_link cookie. Success or account lock deletes it, otherwise it expires after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: In the PostgreSQL user_identities table. UNIQUE(provider, subject) allows one user per Google account, and UNIQUE(user_id, provider) allows one Google account per user.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees the login page message 'Google sign-in failed, try again'. The exchange is not retried, since the code is single-use and the attempt is gone; the user restarts from the button.
haiku-low.q12: The stored attempt mode, login or link, decides the path. Link mode requires the session user to equal the attempt's user_id, otherwise the sign-in-expired error page is shown.

sonnet.q1: Matching is by sub only, so they land in the same account (sub is linked) and get a new session. The changed Gmail address doesn't matter, and Google never changes users.email.
sonnet.q2: The email must be verified (email_verified true) and match a users row (lowercased) with no Google link. Then the user sees Confirm your password and must submit the correct password to POST /auth/google/confirm, with a valid pending record and account not locked. Success resets failed_logins, inserts the user_identities row, deletes the pending record and clears the cookie, then start_session runs.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. The 5th wrong password locks the account for 15 minutes (locked_until = now + 15 min, counter reset) and deletes the pending link and cookie. It shows Account temporarily locked. The user must start Google sign-in again after the lock. Nothing is linked and no session is created.
sonnet.q4: If the email is verified and matches no user: in one transaction a new user is inserted (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) plus a user_identities row, then a session starts. If email_verified is false: redirect to /login with a message to use email and password; nothing is written.
sonnet.q5: Both cases give the same outcome. The attempt record is gone (it expired after the 10 min TTL, or the first callback already deleted it by GETDEL), so the user sees an error page saying sign-in expired or invalid, try again. Nothing is written.
sonnet.q6: It calls the existing start_session(user_id). The old sid's sessions row is deleted, a new sessions row is inserted and a new sid cookie is set (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days, slid forward on use). The user is redirected to next if it is a relative path on the site, else /home.
sonnet.q7: No password or email match is required, and the emails may differ. The session user must equal the attempt's user_id, otherwise it shows the error page. If the sub is already linked to another user, Settings shows that this Google account is linked to another account, and nothing is inserted. If it is already linked to this user, it shows already linked.
sonnet.q8: They are kept server-side in Redis under oidc:attempt:<state> with a 10 min TTL, holding mode, user_id (link only), nonce, code_verifier and next. The callback deletes it with an atomic GETDEL as its first step. Unused records expire.
sonnet.q9: It is held in Redis as oidc:pending:<id> (TTL 10 min), holding user_id, google_sub, google_email and next. The browser holds only the random <id> in an HttpOnly, Secure pending_link cookie. It is deleted when the link succeeds or the account locks, and otherwise expires.
sonnet.q10: In the new PostgreSQL table user_identities (user_id, provider='google', subject = Google sub, email_at_link, linked_at). UNIQUE(provider, subject) gives one user per Google account. UNIQUE(user_id, provider) gives one Google account per user.
sonnet.q11: The user is redirected to /login with the message that Google sign-in failed, try again. The exchange is not retried, because the code is single-use and the attempt record is already deleted. The user starts again from the button. Nothing is written.
sonnet.q12: The attempt record's mode field (login or link) tells it apart. In link mode the record stores user_id, and the callback checks that the current session user equals that user_id. If it doesn't, it shows the expired/invalid error page and links nothing.
